conventions: εὐθέως at the end of MAT.25.15 is a rule 37 versification split between the projection and the ASV: the token stands in 25:15 and its English is the opening 'Straightway' of 25:16. The token is its own `unrepresented` unit in 25:15 and 'Straightway' is `added` in 25:16, each naming the other verse. Do not stretch a nearby English phrase over the token to avoid an empty target. A reference comparison reports it as a disagreement and that report is not a correction.

ἐφ᾽ ὅσον → 'Inasmuch as' (25:40, 25:45) is one `aligned` unit, source head on ὅσον and target head on 'Inasmuch'. Rule 94's precondition is met by its spelt-apart-lexeme clause: 'inasmuch as' is one fixed English clause-introducer whose parts answer to both tokens, 'in-' to the preposition and 'as much as' to the correlative. Do not split it across the two and do not reach for `noncompositional`.

In the verbless relative ὁ τὰ δύο (τάλαντα) at 25:17 and 25:22 the ASV supplies the lexical verb 'received'. Under rules 62 and 96 it rides with the predicate nominal — δύο where no noun is expressed, τάλαντα where one is — discontinuously under rule 15, and never with the determiner-carrying article; it is not `added`. Where the participle λαβών or εἰληφώς is expressed (25:16, 25:18, 25:20, 25:24) nothing is supplied and rule 32's ordinary split applies.

ποτίζω rendered 'gave … drink' (25:35, 25:37, 25:42) is one `aligned` unit headed on 'drink' under rule 91: 'drink' glosses the lexeme and 'gave' is the empty support verb. Any supplied object rides inside the unit under rule 74's contrast, discontinuously under rule 15.

τῶν ἐλαχίστων is analysed differently at 25:40 and 25:45 because the ASV differs, not because the chapter split. 25:40 writes a second 'these' for the article, which takes it under rule 60; 25:45 writes only one, already spent on τούτων, so its article is `unrepresented` under rules 38 and 23. The appositional 'even*' at 25:40 is its own `added` unit under rule 105's substantival-article arm, the article keeping only its own determiner and nothing else.
report: Read all 46 verses end to end rather than relying on the candidate table, which is keyed by source lemma and so cannot see this chapter's four `added` units or its three folded supplied-word decisions. No construction is analysed two ways without the Greek or the ASV licensing the difference. No patches.

Cleared near-misses. (a) A substantival ὁ splits from its participle at 25:16, 25:18, 25:20, 25:24, 25:28 and 25:29, and keeps the discontinuous 'he … that' at 25:10, 25:17 and 25:22 — rule 32 against its own contrast, turning on whether a participle stands. (b) ὥσπερ takes the whole supplied frame 'it is as when' at 25:14 and a bare 'as' at 25:32; 25:32's comparative clause has an expressed finite verb and 25:14's does not. (c) Supplied temporal subordinators ride on participles at 25:3, 25:5 and 25:10 but on ὥσπερ at 25:14, where the participle is already rendered as a bare participle and the 'when' introduces the finite clause of ἐκάλεσεν. (d) τῶν ἐλαχίστων is aligned to a supplied 'these' at 25:40 and unrepresented at 25:45 because the ASV writes two 'these' in one verse and one in the other.

Also uniform on inspection: ἀποδημέω (25:14, 25:15), συνάγω 'took … in' (25:35, 25:38, 25:43), ποτίζω 'gave … drink' (25:35, 25:37, 25:42), αἴρω 'take/taken away' (25:28, 25:29), every rule 106 preverb particle, every article+numeral+noun group under rule 13, every rule 88 supplied juncture, and the rule 20/38/47/54 article-emptying grounds, which are stated separately wherever two of them meet in one verse.

BSB: 12 disagreements, none a genuine error. Nine are the documented convention difference — articles displaced by a possessive, a demonstrative, ἴδιος or σός (25:1, 25:7, 25:21, 25:23, 25:25, 25:30, 25:34, 25:45) and δέ the ASV leaves unwritten (25:11, 25:15). εὐθέως at 25:15 is the rule 37 versification split and that report is not a correction. αὐτοῦ at 25:29 is the chapter's one genuinely contested edge: the ASV writes a single 'him' for τοῦ … ἔχοντος and ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ, rule 32 requires the article to supply the pronoun its relative clause is predicated of, and the unit's note already names the competing reading. Left as accepted.

One single-verse judgment reviewed and left standing, since it is not a cross-verse split and carries its own note: 25:27 gives 'my' to the expressed nominative ἐγώ and the supplied 'I' to ἐκομισάμην. Reading ἐγώ → 'I' with 'my' as a rule 7 helper on the nominalized ἐλθών, or as one discontinuous ἐγώ unit under rule 76, both remain defensible. A later reader wanting to revisit the verse should start there.

No promotion. The two candidates — rule 94's spelt-apart-lexeme clause reaching a two-word subordinator (ἐφ᾽ ὅσον → 'Inasmuch as', two units) and rule 105's article carrier where the article's English is a supplied determiner rather than a pronoun (25:40, one unit) — each follow from the cited rule's own reasoning without widening it, and the corpus supplied here covers neither lemma, so there is no precedent to carry them.
